title: test-0106-MAT-TRIANGLEPROPS
passage: Rohan was drawing triangles in his notebook to understand their properties. He drew a large triangle and a small one, then measured their angles. He mistakenly thought that the larger triangle must have a bigger angle sum than the smaller one. However, his teacher explained that the sum of all three interior angles of any triangle is always exactly 180 degrees, regardless of its size. Rohan then drew an exterior angle by extending one side of his triangle. He initially guessed that this exterior angle must equal the sum of all three interior angles, but he learned it actually equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles. Next, he tried to form a triangle using sticks of lengths 3 cm, 4 cm, and 7 cm. He thought they would connect, but the teacher showed that the sum of two sides must be strictly greater than the third side for a triangle to exist. Finally, Rohan looked at a right-angled triangle with legs of 3 cm and 4 cm. He tried to find the hypotenuse by adding the two legs to get 7 cm, but the Pythagoras property states that the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the two legs, making the hypotenuse 5 cm.
summary: He thought the larger triangle had a bigger angle sum than the smaller one. However, his teacher explained that the sum of all three interior angles of any triangle is always exactly 180 degrees, regardless of its size. Rohan drew an exterior angle by extending one side of his triangle.
